newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria sells 17.58 bln levs 1- and 4-wk T-bills.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria sells 17.58 bln levs 1- and 4-wk T-bills.

text.p: Bulgaria's Finance Ministry on Wednesday sold two discount T-bill issues with maturities of one week and four weeks, yielding 3.81 percent and 17.76 percent to maturity, respectively, the central bank said.
Bids were received for a total of 17.618 billion levs of T-bills but the ministry approved bids for 17.578 billion levs worth of paper.
The issues were offered with no par value or minimum acceptable price set in advance by the ministry. Auction dates and maturity dates for both issues overlap.
Details of the issues follow. Prices are in percent of par:
Bids received 7,357.6 million levs 10,260.2 million levs
Bids approved 7,317.6 million levs 10,260.2 million levs
Avg yield to maturity 3.81 pct 17.76 pct
"Banks showed higher interest in four-week paper today probably due to expectations of a continuing lev rise," a money market dealer said.
Two four-week discount T-bill issues were not sold two weeks ago due to a lack of bids as the lev was falling sharply.

Today it advanced to 2,220-2,250 per dollar at close from 2,500-2,550 at the opening and 2,660-2,720 at the previous close as dollar supply rose on expectations of further lev gains. It traded near 2,800 on Monday.
